title: SunPark people-ops conversational prototype diary
content:
Meeting: 2026-01-14 (intro + technical discovery)
Attendees: Maya (SunPark PO), Samir (SunPark Eng), Ava (RE solutions), Ethan (RE systems), Priya (RE security)

Quick context / ask:
- SunPark wants a lightweight conversational HR assistant for employees to ask policy/benefits/leave questions. Target: internal-only, behind Okta, single-tenant (SunPark VPC).
- Primary sources: Workday (payroll/time off), internal HR wiki (Confluence pages), benefits PDFs, and a small FAQ spreadsheet.
- Goals: reduce tier-1 HR tickets, serve 80% of common queries, escalate to live HR for ambiguous cases.
- Timeline: pilot for 500 employees in Q2; broader rollout TBD.

Constraints called out by SunPark:
- PII + payroll data: cannot leave VPC. Any sensitive tokens or message text containing payroll identifiers must be retained for <=30 days and then rotated/erased per SunPark policy.
- No external third-party model hosting for PII queries — they want Redwood Private (VPC) with optional on-prem later.
- SSO: Okta SAML for auth; user identity must be passed to app layer but redacted from logs stored outside VPC.
- Workday integration: read-only API token; SunPark will provide scoped service account with narrow scopes.
- Latency expectation: p95 < 350ms for short (one-shot) queries; interactive chat OK up to 800ms per chunk, but they'd like lower.
- Cost sensitivity: pilot budget small; prefer smaller model family (quantized) if quality ok, otherwise fallback to larger model for complex queries.

Notes on model / data strategy (brainstorm):
- Index embeddings for Confluence + benefits PDFs; use per-tenant embedding store inside VPC (we suggested Vector DB inside VPC or local file-backed index).
- Two-tier approach: (1) safe-surface via symmetric retrieval + deterministic templates for facts (policy text, leave balances from Workday), (2) open generation for conversational tone.
- For payroll/time-off lookups, avoid LLM hallucinating — implement deterministic data lookup path that returns structured JSON and then lightweight templating for response. Return: {avl_days: 8, last_request: 2025-12-18, policy_link: ...} (we'll mock shape).
- Consider model gating: if retrieved facts suffice (high match score) -> deterministic response w/ citation; else -> generative assistant with fallback to human.

Privacy / audit / logs:
- Audit logs must capture event id, user-id (hashed when stored outside VPC), query-vector-hash, timestamp, flow (retrieval vs generation) and redaction token markers.
- Redwood console telemetry is acceptable for performance metrics but must not store raw user queries containing specified PII fields. Need KMS integration and field-level redaction hooks from SunPark.
- Retention policy: short-term (30d) for troubleshooting, then automatic purge. Confirm whether Redwood can expose auto-purge APIs for Private deployment (action item).

Integration details / gotchas observed in call:
- Workday rate limits: SunPark's Workday API enforces 30 calls/min per service account. Need caching strategy (per-user TTL for balance queries 2min) and batching for bulk lookups (payroll reports).
- Confluence pages inconsistent headings; embedding quality degraded by boilerplate sections. Suggest preprocessing: strip nav/headers, extract policy sections heuristically, normalize date formats.
- Okta session token lifetime short (5m default) -> session refresh handshake with Redwood client must support silent reauth or token exchange.
- Benefit PDFs are scanned for some legacy plans (OCR noise). We'll ask SunPark for original digital copies; otherwise run OCR cleanup pipeline (low-priority).
- Edge-case: manager-level queries (compensation comparators) flagged as high-risk; SunPark wants explicit escalation and logging for these. Need policy classifier to flag sensitive intents.

Prompting / evaluation plan (rough):
- Seed prompt templates for common intents: time-off balance, leave policy, parental leave eligibility, 401k enrollment windows. Keep templates strict for numeric or policy outputs.
- Build small eval set (~60 prompts) from real historical tickets (SunPark will redact) to test model/regression. Track quality metrics: accuracy (exact-match for numeric), citation recall, hallucination rate.
- Metrics dashboard: p95 latency, tokens per request, failover count to fallback model, human escalation rate.

Performance and architecture suggestions:
- Dedicated small cluster in VPC (2x T4g or equivalently sized GPUs) for baseline pilot. Use Redwood's prefix caching for common prompt patterns to reduce token costs.
- Autoscale policy: maintain 5 concurrent sessions p99, scale quickly for spikes (rate-based). Since Workday is rate-limited, limit LLM call bursts by queueing/aggregation layer.

Open questions (to confirm):
- SunPark expects payroll queries to remain entirely inside VPC — do they also want embeddings never to leave VPC? (asked -> yes).
- Who is SunPark's KMS provider? (they mentioned AWS KMS; confirm CMKs + rotation windows).
- Level of logging allowed to be visible to Redwood SREs for incident debug (they prefer minimal; need to define incident-only access flow).
- Are managers allowed to request compensation benchmarking through this assistant? (they said no by default, escalate to HR).

Immediate action items (owners + rough dates):
- A: Send Redwood secure intake form for VPC onboarding & KMS info to SunPark (Ava) — due 2026-01-20.
- B: Create privacy checklist for fields to redact (SSN, bank acct, employee ID) and implement draft redaction pipeline for Private deployment (Priya) — due 2026-01-28.
- C: Spike: local embeddings PoC inside a sandbox VPC using 1k Confluence pages + 50 PDFs; test retrieval precision and citation display (Ethan + Diego) — start 2026-01-18, report by 2026-02-05.
- D: Draft integration spec for Workday (rate limits, fields, token refresh pattern) and share with SunPark eng (Ava) — due 2026-01-22 (JIRA RED-5128).
- E: Create 60-eval-prompt set and baseline runs (small model quantized + medium model) for initial quality/cost tradeoffs (Priya + Ethan) — due 2026-02-12.
- F: Confirm Okta session flow and sample token exchange with SunPark (Samir) — due 2026-01-21.

Prototype ideas / quick wins:
- Slack command fallback: /hr-balance -> quick read from Workday + templated response; low-lift, visible value.
- Email digest: weekly summary of escalations to HR to track reduction in tickets.
- Policy quick-links: markup of Confluence pages to show 'short answer' snippet + link to source (helps auditability).

Risks flagged:
- Hallucination on policy nuance -> requires strict retrieval-first design and clear disambiguation flow.
- Workday rate limits + concurrent employees -> potential queueing backlog during open enrollment; need prefetch strategy for scheduled campaigns.
- OCRed PDFs may poison embeddings -> preprocessing needed.

Notes to self / informal:
- SunPark is small but conservative — push for Private onboarding early; Dedicated-hosted mix might be acceptable for non-PII queries (ask them if they'd accept hosted for generic FAQ).
- Keep eval set heavy on numeric questions (balances/dates) so we can detect silent regressions.
- Remember to ask about labour law locales (employees in EU vs US might have different policy text).

Next sync: schedule 30m follow-up week of 2026-01-25 to review PoC results + confirm Workday token details.

Misc links and quick refs pasted from call:
- SunPark HR wiki (shared): https://sunpark.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/HR
- Workday API spec they referenced: https://docs.workday.com/dev/api/reference (SunPark will provide client ID + scopes)

End diary entry.

(Will update with PoC notes and initial eval runs — stub for tracking RED-5128.)
